question: Under 20 CSR 2250-8.160, how long must a Missouri broker retain true copies of business books, accounts (including voided checks), records, contracts, brokerage relationship agreements, closing statements, and correspondence relating to each real estate transaction the broker has handled?
choice_a: At least three years
choice_b: At least one year
choice_c: At least five years
choice_d: At least seven years
explanation: 20 CSR 2250-8.160(1) requires every broker to retain true copies of the listed transaction records for a period of at least three years.

question: Under 20 CSR 2250-8.160, retained transaction records must be made available for inspection by the Missouri Real Estate Commission and its authorized agents when?
choice_a: Only after 30 days' written notice from the commission
choice_b: At all times during usual business hours at the broker's regular place of business
choice_c: Only during a scheduled annual audit
choice_d: Only if the commission obtains a subpoena
explanation: 20 CSR 2250-8.160(1) requires records to be available for commission inspection at all times during usual business hours at the broker's regular place of business.

question: May a Missouri broker charge a client a separate fee for retaining the transaction records required under 20 CSR 2250-8.160?
choice_a: Yes, up to $25 per closed file
choice_b: Yes, if the fee is disclosed in the listing agreement
choice_c: No, the rule expressly states no broker shall charge a separate fee relating to retention of records
choice_d: Yes, but only for records stored electronically
explanation: 20 CSR 2250-8.160(1) states plainly that no broker shall charge a separate fee relating to retention of records.

question: Under 20 CSR 2250-8.160(2), besides retaining property management agreements and related correspondence for three years, what else must a broker retain regarding management activities unless those records are released or transferred?
choice_a: Nothing further beyond the signed agreement itself
choice_b: Only the owner's federal tax filings
choice_c: Only monthly bank statements, with no requirement to retain the agreement
choice_d: All business books, accounts, and records relating to the management activities, unless released to the owner(s) or transferred to another broker by a written detailed receipt or transmittal letter agreed to in writing by all parties
explanation: 20 CSR 2250-8.160(2) requires the broker to also retain all business books, accounts, and records for management activities unless they are released or transferred as described.

question: Before a Missouri licensee may rent or lease, list for rent, negotiate a lease, or show a property to prospective renters, what must the licensee's broker hold under 20 CSR 2250-8.200?
choice_a: A current written property management agreement or other written authorization signed by the owner or the owner's authorized agent
choice_b: Only a verbal understanding with the property owner
choice_c: A copy of the owner's mortgage payoff statement
choice_d: Only a listing agreement authorizing sale of the property
explanation: 20 CSR 2250-8.200(1) prohibits property management leasing activity unless the broker holds a current written property management agreement or other written authorization signed by the owner or the owner's authorized agent.

question: Under 20 CSR 2250-8.200(2), may a licensee who is managing the leasing or rental of real estate also act as an agent in the sale or exchange of that same property?
choice_a: No, a property manager may never also act as a sales agent for the same property
choice_b: Yes, but only if the licensee complies with the brokerage service agreement requirements of 20 CSR 2250-8.090
choice_c: Yes, with no additional requirement of any kind
choice_d: Only with the Missouri Real Estate Commission's individualized written pre-approval
explanation: 20 CSR 2250-8.200(2) permits this dual role provided the licensee complies with the brokerage service agreement requirements of 20 CSR 2250-8.090.

question: Under 20 CSR 2250-8.220(1), what must a Missouri broker who manages rental property establish and maintain, separate from other trust funds, for the deposit of current rents and money received for property management expenses?
choice_a: A single combined escrow account used interchangeably for sales earnest money and rentals
choice_b: A branch-office petty cash fund
choice_c: A separate escrow account (or accounts) designated as a property management escrow account
choice_d: An interest-bearing personal savings account in the broker's own name
explanation: 20 CSR 2250-8.220(1) requires a broker to establish and maintain a separate escrow account designated as a property management escrow account.

question: Under 20 CSR 2250-8.220(2), where must a Missouri broker maintain security deposits received in connection with property management?
choice_a: Commingled directly with the property management escrow account for administrative convenience
choice_b: In the broker's personal operating account
choice_c: Returned to the tenant automatically within 10 days of receipt
choice_d: Intact, in an escrow account other than the property management escrow account, unless the owner(s) have agreed otherwise in writing
explanation: 20 CSR 2250-8.220(2) requires security deposits to be held intact in an escrow account separate from the property management escrow account, pursuant to section 339.105, RSMo, unless the owner(s) agree otherwise in writing.

question: Under 20 CSR 2250-8.220(3), within how many banking days must a broker deposit money received in connection with property management into the broker's escrow or trust account?
choice_a: Ten banking days
choice_b: Three banking days
choice_c: Thirty banking days
choice_d: Five banking days
explanation: 20 CSR 2250-8.220(3) requires deposit within ten banking days of receipt.

question: Under 20 CSR 2250-8.220(4), what must a property manager (licensee) do with money received in connection with property management?
choice_a: Deposit it directly into the property owner's personal bank account
choice_b: Immediately deliver it to the supervising broker
choice_c: Hold it for up to 10 days before delivering it to the broker
choice_d: Deposit it into the broker's general operating account
explanation: 20 CSR 2250-8.220(4) requires a property manager to immediately deliver to the supervising broker all money received in connection with property management.

question: Under 20 CSR 2250-8.220(5), what type of financial institution must hold a broker's property management escrow account?
choice_a: Any licensed title insurance company
choice_b: A bonded third-party property management firm
choice_c: A bank, savings and loan, or credit union
choice_d: A central depository maintained by the Missouri Real Estate Commission
explanation: 20 CSR 2250-8.220(5) specifies the account must be at a bank, savings and loan, or credit union.

question: Under 20 CSR 2250-8.220(6), absent a different written agreement, how often must fees or commissions payable to a broker be withdrawn from a property management escrow account?
choice_a: At least once a week
choice_b: Only at the end of each lease term
choice_c: Only annually
choice_d: At least once a month
explanation: 20 CSR 2250-8.220(6) requires monthly withdrawal of fees or commissions unless otherwise agreed in writing.

question: Under 20 CSR 2250-8.220(6), rent paid in advance as a deposit for the last month's rent (or as rent other than the current month's rent) held by a broker must generally be deposited into which account?
choice_a: The property management escrow account, unless otherwise agreed to in writing
choice_b: The security deposit escrow account, regardless of any agreement
choice_c: The broker's general operating account
choice_d: An account maintained directly by the Missouri Real Estate Commission
explanation: 20 CSR 2250-8.220(6) directs that such advance rent be deposited in the property management escrow account unless otherwise agreed to in writing.

question: Under 20 CSR 2250-8.220(7), what must a broker execute, upon request of the Missouri Real Estate Commission or its agent, regarding examination of the property management escrow account?
choice_a: A quarterly self-audit certification filed with the county recorder
choice_b: A form entitled "Consent to Examine and Audit Escrow or Trust Account"
choice_c: A surety bond application
choice_d: A notarized inventory of managed properties
explanation: 20 CSR 2250-8.220(7) requires the broker to execute the commission's "Consent to Examine and Audit Escrow or Trust Account" form.

question: Under 20 CSR 2250-8.220(8), what must each check, check stub or other disbursement record, and each deposit ticket on a property management escrow account indicate?
choice_a: Only the broker's license number
choice_b: Only the date of deposit
choice_c: The related transaction
choice_d: Nothing beyond the dollar amount
explanation: 20 CSR 2250-8.220(8) requires each check, disbursement record, and deposit ticket to indicate the related transaction.

question: Under 20 CSR 2250-8.230, disputes over the return of security deposits to lessees are governed by which Missouri statute, in addition to any other applicable law?
choice_a: Section 339.100, RSMo
choice_b: Section 339.780, RSMo
choice_c: Section 407.020, RSMo
choice_d: Section 535.300, RSMo
explanation: 20 CSR 2250-8.230 states that the return of security deposits to lessees and related disputes are governed by section 535.300, RSMo, and any other applicable law.

question: Under 20 CSR 2250-8.090(9), a written property management agreement between a broker and the property owner must specify which of the following regarding funds?
choice_a: Whether security deposits and prepaid rents will be held by the broker or the owner
choice_b: The exact bank routing number of the broker's personal checking account
choice_c: The owner's personal credit score
choice_d: The broker's total annual commission income from all clients
explanation: 20 CSR 2250-8.090(9)(C) requires the property management agreement to specify whether security deposits and prepaid rents will be held by the broker or the owner.

question: Under 20 CSR 2250-8.090(9), besides identifying the managed property and stating the fee or commission terms, what must a written property management agreement contain regarding ending the relationship?
choice_a: A mandatory two-year minimum term with no termination clause permitted
choice_b: The terms and conditions for termination of the property management agreement by the broker or the owner of the property
choice_c: Automatic renewal language with no termination option available
choice_d: Only the owner's right to terminate, with no corresponding right for the broker
explanation: 20 CSR 2250-8.090(9)(E) requires the agreement to provide the terms and conditions for termination by either the broker or the owner.

question: Under 20 CSR 2250-8.090(10), once the owner signs a written property management agreement, what must the licensee do, and what must the licensee's broker retain?
choice_a: Mail a copy to the owner only if the owner requests it within 30 days
choice_b: File the original agreement directly with the Missouri Real Estate Commission instead of keeping a copy
choice_c: Give the owner (or the owner's authorized agent) a legible copy of the agreement at the time the owner's signature is obtained, and the broker must retain a copy of the agreement
choice_d: No copy is required unless the agreement is later renewed
explanation: 20 CSR 2250-8.090(10) requires the licensee to give the owner a legible copy at signing, and requires the licensee's broker to retain a copy of the property management agreement and any signed addendums.

question: Under RSMo 339.105 and 20 CSR 2250-8.120(3), a broker's escrow or trust account (which also holds funds such as security deposits and prepaid rents) must be what type of account?
choice_a: A money market mutual fund
choice_b: A certificate of deposit
choice_c: A cash-only ledger with no bank account required
choice_d: A checking account at a bank, savings and loan, or credit union
explanation: 20 CSR 2250-8.120(3) requires the escrow or trust account maintained under section 339.105, RSMo, to be a checking account in a bank, savings and loan, or credit union.

question: Under 20 CSR 2250-8.090(9)(A), what is the first requirement every written property management agreement or other written authorization between a broker and the owner of real estate must satisfy?
choice_a: It must identify the property to be managed
choice_b: It must state the exact market rent to be charged
choice_c: It must list the tenant's credit score
choice_d: It must be notarized by a Missouri notary public
explanation: 20 CSR 2250-8.090(9)(A) requires the property management agreement to identify the property to be managed.

question: Under 20 CSR 2250-8.090(9)(B), besides identifying the managed property, what must a written property management agreement state regarding compensation?
choice_a: Only the total dollar cap on repair expenditures the broker may authorize
choice_b: The amount of fee or commission to be paid and when the fee or commission will be paid
choice_c: The broker's hourly billing rate for all management activities
choice_d: The commission rate charged by competing brokers in the same market
explanation: 20 CSR 2250-8.090(9)(B) requires the agreement to state the amount of fee or commission to be paid and when it will be paid.

question: Under 20 CSR 2250-8.090(9)(D), in addition to specifying termination terms, what date must a written property management agreement contain?
choice_a: The tenant's move-in date
choice_b: The date the property was originally purchased by the owner
choice_c: The beginning date of the agreement
choice_d: The date of the broker's most recent continuing education renewal
explanation: 20 CSR 2250-8.090(9)(D) requires the property management agreement to contain the beginning date of the agreement.

question: Under 20 CSR 2250-8.090(9)(F), a written property management agreement must include which of the following, in addition to fee, term, and termination provisions?
choice_a: A pre-printed limitation of the broker's liability for any negligence
choice_b: The owner's Social Security number
choice_c: A waiver of the owner's right to terminate for cause
choice_d: The licensee's duties and responsibilities
explanation: 20 CSR 2250-8.090(9)(F) requires the property management agreement to include the licensee's duties and responsibilities.

question: Under 20 CSR 2250-8.090(9)(G), a written property management agreement must contain a statement permitting or prohibiting the designated broker from offering subagency, except in what circumstance?
choice_a: This requirement is not applicable for transaction broker agreements
choice_b: This requirement applies only to commercial property management agreements
choice_c: This requirement is waived whenever the owner resides out of state
choice_d: This requirement is waived if the property has fewer than four rental units
explanation: 20 CSR 2250-8.090(9)(G) requires a statement permitting or prohibiting subagency, but expressly notes this is not applicable for transaction broker agreements.

question: Under 20 CSR 2250-8.090(9)(K), a written property management agreement must contain a statement confirming what?
choice_a: That the landlord waived all rights to receive a Broker Disclosure Form
choice_b: That the landlord received the Broker Disclosure Form prescribed by the commission, either on or before signing the agreement or upon the licensee obtaining any personal or financial information, whichever occurs first
choice_c: That the tenant, not the landlord, received the Broker Disclosure Form
choice_d: That the Broker Disclosure Form will be provided only upon the landlord's written request
explanation: 20 CSR 2250-8.090(9)(K) requires the agreement to contain a statement confirming the landlord received the Broker Disclosure Form by the earlier of signing the agreement or the licensee obtaining personal or financial information.

question: Under 20 CSR 2250-8.090(9)(M), what is required of any addendums, riders, endorsements, or attachments to a property management agreement?
choice_a: They must be filed with the Missouri Real Estate Commission within 10 days of execution
choice_b: They may be signed by the property manager alone, without the owner's signature
choice_c: They must contain the signatures of all the owners and the broker or affiliated licensee as authorized by the broker
choice_d: They need only be initialed by the tenant, not signed by the owner or broker
explanation: 20 CSR 2250-8.090(9)(M) requires addendums, riders, endorsements, or attachments to the property management agreement to contain the signatures of all owners and the broker or affiliated licensee.

question: Under 20 CSR 2250-8.220(1), before making disbursements from a property management escrow account, what must a broker ensure?
choice_a: That the Missouri Real Estate Commission has pre-approved the disbursement in writing
choice_b: That the disbursement is made only in cash
choice_c: That the tenant has co-signed the disbursement check
choice_d: That the account balance attributable to that owner's property (or properties) is sufficient to cover the disbursements
explanation: 20 CSR 2250-8.220(1) requires a broker to ensure the account balance for that owner's property(ies) is sufficient to cover disbursements before making them, preventing one owner's funds from being used to cover another owner's expenses.

question: Under 20 CSR 2250-8.220(8), a check written on a property management escrow account for a licensee's fee or commission must be made payable to whom?
choice_a: The licensee who is owed the fee or commission, or to the firm's general operating account
choice_b: Cash, so it can be split among multiple licensees
choice_c: The tenant, who then forwards it to the licensee
choice_d: The Missouri Real Estate Commission directly
explanation: 20 CSR 2250-8.220(8) requires a check written on the escrow account for licensee fees or commission to be made payable to the licensee who is owed the fee or commission or to the firm's general operating account.

question: Under RSMo 535.300.1, what is the maximum security deposit a Missouri landlord may demand or receive from a tenant?
choice_a: An amount not in excess of one month's rent
choice_b: An amount not in excess of two months' rent
choice_c: An amount not in excess of three months' rent
choice_d: There is no statutory cap on the amount of a security deposit
explanation: RSMo 535.300.1 prohibits a landlord from demanding or receiving a security deposit in excess of two months' rent.

question: Under RSMo 535.300.2, where must a Missouri landlord hold a tenant's security deposit, and who is generally entitled to any interest it earns?
choice_a: In an uninsured private trust account, with any interest paid to the tenant
choice_b: In a joint account requiring the tenant's signature for any withdrawal
choice_c: In an institution whose accounts are insured by an agency of the federal government, with the landlord generally entitled to keep any interest earned
choice_d: In cash on the landlord's premises, with no interest accruing
explanation: RSMo 535.300.2 requires security deposits to be held in a federally insured institution and generally allows the landlord to retain interest earned, except for deposits held by certain government housing authorities.

question: Under RSMo 535.300.3, within how many days after termination of a tenancy must a Missouri landlord either return the full security deposit or furnish the tenant a written itemized list of damages?
choice_a: Ten days
choice_b: Sixty days
choice_c: Forty-five days
choice_d: Thirty days
explanation: RSMo 535.300.3 requires a landlord to return the deposit in full or furnish a written itemized list of damages within thirty days after the tenancy terminates.

question: Under RSMo 535.300.4, which of the following may a Missouri landlord NOT deduct from a tenant's security deposit?
choice_a: Damage caused by ordinary wear and tear
choice_b: Unpaid rent owed by the tenant
choice_c: The cost of restoring the unit to its move-in condition, reasonable wear and tear excepted
choice_d: Damages resulting from the tenant's failure to give adequate notice to terminate
explanation: RSMo 535.300.4 permits deductions for unpaid rent, restoring the unit to move-in condition (ordinary wear and tear excepted), agreed-upon carpet cleaning, and damages from inadequate termination notice, but ordinary wear and tear itself may not be charged against the deposit.

question: Under RSMo 535.300.5, what right does a Missouri tenant have regarding the landlord's move-out inspection of the rental unit?
choice_a: The tenant has no right to attend any move-out inspection
choice_b: The tenant has the right to be present at the inspection if the landlord gives written notice of its timing to the tenant's last known address
choice_c: The tenant may conduct the inspection alone, without the landlord present
choice_d: The tenant must hire a licensed home inspector to attend on the tenant's behalf
explanation: RSMo 535.300.5 requires the landlord to give written notice of the inspection timing to the tenant's last known address and entitles the tenant to be present at the inspection.

question: Under RSMo 535.300.6, what remedy is available to a Missouri tenant if the landlord wrongfully withholds all or part of a security deposit?
choice_a: The tenant may only recover the exact amount wrongfully withheld, with no additional penalty
choice_b: The tenant forfeits any right to recover once thirty days have passed
choice_c: The tenant may recover as damages twice the amount wrongfully withheld
choice_d: The tenant's sole remedy is to file a complaint with the Missouri Real Estate Commission
explanation: RSMo 535.300.6 allows a tenant to recover as damages twice the amount wrongfully withheld when a landlord wrongfully withholds a security deposit.

question: Under RSMo 535.300.7, which of the following is true regarding a tenant's security deposit and rent obligations?
choice_a: A tenant may always apply the security deposit toward the final month's rent instead of paying rent
choice_b: A landlord is barred from recovering any damages beyond the amount of the security deposit
choice_c: The statute requires the landlord to apply the deposit to the last month's rent automatically
choice_d: The statute does not entitle a tenant to apply the security deposit as payment of rent, and does not bar a landlord from pursuing damages exceeding the deposit amount
explanation: RSMo 535.300.7 clarifies that nothing in the section entitles a tenant to apply the deposit toward rent, nor does it prevent a landlord from seeking damages in excess of the deposit.

question: Under RSMo 535.300.8's definition of "security deposit," which of the following is expressly excluded from the definition?
choice_a: A pet deposit
choice_b: The last month's rent paid in advance
choice_c: Money held to cover unpaid utility bills
choice_d: Money held to cover agreed-upon carpet cleaning costs
explanation: RSMo 535.300.8 defines security deposit as money or property held to secure performance under a rental agreement, but expressly excludes a pet deposit from that definition.

question: Under 20 CSR 2250-8.090(9)(H), a written property management agreement must contain a statement addressing which of the following?
choice_a: Whether the tenant is permitted to sublease the property without the owner's written consent
choice_b: Whether the designated broker and/or affiliated licensee is permitted or prohibited from acting as a disclosed dual agent, and if permitted, the duties and responsibilities of a dual agent
choice_c: Whether the owner is permitted to terminate the agreement without cause at any time before its stated ending date
choice_d: Whether the property may be shown to prospective buyers without a signed listing agreement
explanation: 20 CSR 2250-8.090(9)(H) requires the property management agreement to contain a statement permitting or prohibiting the designated broker and/or affiliated licensee from acting as a disclosed dual agent, and if permitted, to state the duties and responsibilities of a dual agent.

question: Under 20 CSR 2250-8.090(9)(I), besides addressing subagency and dual agency, a written property management agreement must also contain a statement addressing what?
choice_a: Whether the broker is permitted to charge the owner a late fee for delinquent rent payments
choice_b: Whether the owner is permitted to hire a second, competing property manager for the same property
choice_c: Whether the designated broker and/or affiliated licensee is permitted or prohibited from acting as a transaction broker, and if permitted, the duties and responsibilities of a transaction broker
choice_d: Whether the tenant is permitted to keep pets on the managed property
explanation: 20 CSR 2250-8.090(9)(I) requires the property management agreement to contain a statement permitting or prohibiting the designated broker and/or affiliated licensee from acting as a transaction broker, and if permitted, to state the duties and responsibilities of a transaction broker.

question: Under 20 CSR 2250-8.090(9)(J), a written property management agreement must include specification of whether the designated broker is authorized to do what?
choice_a: Sell the managed property to a third party without first notifying the owner
choice_b: Waive the owner's right to receive an accounting of rents collected
choice_c: Assign the property management agreement to any other broker without the owner's written consent
choice_d: Cooperate with and compensate other designated brokers acting pursuant to any other brokerage relationship defined by sections 339.710 to 339.860, RSMo, including but not limited to tenant's agents and/or transaction brokers
explanation: 20 CSR 2250-8.090(9)(J) requires the agreement to specify whether the designated broker is authorized to cooperate with and compensate other designated brokers acting pursuant to any other brokerage relationship defined by sections 339.710 to 339.860, RSMo, including tenant's agents and/or transaction brokers.

question: Under 20 CSR 2250-8.090(9)(L), separate from the signature requirement imposed on any addendums, riders, endorsements, or attachments under subsection (M), what must the written property management agreement itself contain?
choice_a: The signatures of all the owners and the broker or affiliated licensee as authorized by the broker
choice_b: Only the tenant's signature, with no signature required from the owner
choice_c: A notarized acknowledgment executed before a Missouri notary public
choice_d: The signature of the Missouri Real Estate Commission's executive director
explanation: 20 CSR 2250-8.090(9)(L) requires the property management agreement itself to contain the signatures of all the owners and the broker or affiliated licensee as authorized by the broker, while subsection (M) separately imposes the same signature requirement on any addendums, riders, endorsements, or attachments to the agreement.
